steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).

Whisk flour, baking soda, and salt together in a bowl until thoroughly combined. Beat sugar and butter together in a separate large bowl with an electric mixer until creamy, about 5 minutes. Add eggs, one at a time, beating well after each addition. Beat in lemon zest, lemon juice, and vanilla extract. Gently mix in flour mixture until just incorporated. Chill dough about 30 minutes.
Roll dough into balls, about 1 ½ teaspoonfuls per cookie; place about 2 inches apart onto baking sheets.
Bake in the preheated oven until set and just beginning to brown at edges, about 8 minutes; cool on baking sheets for 1 minute before transferring to wire racks to cool.

raw_recipe.headline: Princess Cookies
raw_recipe.description: This princess cookie recipe yields delicate lemon cookies — drizzle them with a confectioners' sugar and lemon juice glaze or roll in sugar, then bake.

review.reviewBody: I am the recipe submitter- for those of you that have been curious about the story that I'm referring to, it is out of an old Sesame Street alphabet book that was mine when I was a child. The recipe was my own creation, but the story was the inspiration. :). Hope this helps.

Light and lemony! A delicate, sweet little cookie that's perfect for any little princess to enjoy at tea parties along with her "imaginary" friends. These are so easy to make and while they aren't crisp but are more spongy and cake-like cookies they are none the less delicious. I did a lemon glaze on some, rolled a few in turbinado sugar before baking, and dusted others with powdered sugar just to change it up a bit. Overall, very good little cookies.

Definitely takes longer than 8 minutes to get them to a solid consistency. But if you use two smaller meyer lemons {zest and juice} the flavor will definitely be there. Scooped them a little bit bigger and flattened them just a bit on the sheet. Baked for roughly 13 minutes or until they felt set. Yummy :D

These cookies definitely need the lemon glaze on top. The texture is nice, but if you are looking for a strong lemon flavor you probably need to add more lemon zest (I added the zest of 4 lemons in the cookie and one in the glaze!). Sitting overnight really helped bring out the lemon flavor. I found the dough was much less sticky and the cookies held their shape better if the dough chilled at least an hour.

I love these cookies! they are easy and fabulous. I used half butter and half canola oil to have less lactose. I dropped small spoonfuls, I'm too lazy to roll cookies! I fit 16 to a pan. When cool, I drizzled them with the juice and zest from one lemon mixed with powdered sugar. The last ones got a little stale by the end of the week, so next time I'll freeze some.

I used fresh lemons & zest. A small scoop was just right. Watch so they don't get too brown. I drizzled glaze made with 1 cup powdered sugar, lemon zest and enough fresh lemon juice to get the right consistency. Delicious & pretty!

I made these cookies in honor of our dear Marianne's Birthday in January. They are a very easy "shortbread" type cookie or butter cookie with a hint of lemon. I did like them very much, but was expecting a real HIT of lemon flavor and it just wasn't that lemon-y. That's the ONLY reason I gave this recipe 4 Stars instead of 5. Next time, I think I'll use more lemon juice and zest. And, I also think I'll ice them with a lemon glaze next time too. They are worthy of making again.

Really tasty! A little spongy and soft for my intent (shipping half way across the globe) but darn tasty for home. I made a simple syrup of Lemon Juice and white sugar, dipped a fork in it, and pressed each dough ball down with the dipped fork, and it made a nice little crunchy pattern on top. I then drizzled the syrup on the cookies fresh out of the oven. YUMMY!

THESE ARE AMAZING!!!! I made them with slightly more lemon juice (about a teaspoon) and they came out wonderful. Due to me being lazy, I used a scoop (1 1/2 tbs) to shape the cookies and I had to cook them for 13 minutes instead of 8. They still turned out awesome. :)

Very good cookie. Definitely will be using the again. However, others have said it, it needs a boost in the lemon department. Its a very, very subtle lemon flavor. I kicked it up a notch by doing a lemon zest glaze. The lemon glaze goes well with the sweet, light lemon cookie.

I substituted the lemon juice with 2 TBSP of Orange Liqueur and didn't add any zest. Absolutely delicious. I also didn't wait 30 minutes to chill the dough. These babies turned out amazing. However I also added some icing to the cookies: confectioner sugar with orange liqueur....man oh man!!

This recipe is super simple to follow and the cookies taste amazing with coffee or tea. They're soft, moist and cake-like if you make them bigger (see pics). So, you don't need a box cake mix like other recipes. I prefer to make everything from scratch. The only thing I tweaked was using: Whole Earth's Plant-Based Sugar Alternative ➡️Erythritol & Monk Fruit. It tastes like white sugar but is healthier! I made a simple glaze with 1+cup of powdered sugar til thicken, a tbsp of unsalted butter, & 1/3 cup fresh squeezed lemon juice, blended with a small hand mixer.
It wasn't bad, the cookies just really dried out after a few days

I have been making these cookies for over a decade. They are perfectly light and sweet. A drizzle of glaze made with powdered sugar, lemon juice, and zest take them to the next level. So glad they have a unique name so I can always search for "Princess Cookies" and find this recipe!
I have been making these cookies for several years and everyone always loves them overtime I make them
Mediocre flavor . Had to cook them much longer than the recipe called for. I’m sad, I was so excited to try these!
Finished product looks nothing like pictured cookies. Missing instructions for sugar and glaze.
It was great and I had fun making it. My dad helped me make it. and we loved it. -Kyla A.
I put Swedish Fish in the dough right before putting in the oven, and they were super delicious! My dad just really likes Swedish Fish!
